summary: CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION NEW DELHI Petition No. 294/TD/2026 Coram: Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member Date of Order: 29th October, 2026 In the matter of Application under Sections 14(c), 15 and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 15(1) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2020, seeking upgradation of the existing Category ‘II’ Inter-State Trading Licence to Category ‘I’ Inter-State Trading Licence. And In the matter of RPG Power Trading Company Limited, 6 Church Lane, 1st Floor, Kolkata - 700001, West Bengal. Applicant Parties present: Ms. Divya Chaturvedi, Advocate, RPTCL ORDER The Applicant, RPG Power Trading Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as “RPGPTCL”), has filed the present application to upgrade its inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category ‘II’ to Category ‘I’. 2. Vide order dated 23.9.2008 in Petition No. 85/2008, the Applicant was granted an inter-State trading licence as a Category ‘E’ electricity trader throughout India, in accordance with the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms Order in Petition No. 294/TD/2026 Page 1 of 8 and Conditions for Grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2004. The Category ‘E’ licensee was first classified as a Category ‘I’ licensee under the Trading Licence Regulations, 2009 and thereafter, through the first amendment to the Trading Licence Regulations, 2009, the Category ‘I’ licensee was reclassified as a Category ‘II’ licensee. 3. Pursuant to the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for grant of Trading Licence and other related matters) Regulations, 2009 (hereinafter referred to as the “Trading Licence Regulations, 2009”), which came into effect on 16.2.2009, the existing Category ‘E’ licensees were converted into Category ‘II’ licensees. 4. The Applicant has submitted that, considering the expected rise in trading volume on the Petitioner’s platform and its future business potential, it is seeking upgradation of its existing Category ‘II’ licence to Category ‘I’ licence. The proposed upgradation would enable the Applicant to trade electricity across inter-State boundaries without volume restrictions, expand its participation in business opportunities presently limited by its current licence category, and further strengthen its role in the national power market and grid stability. Hearing Dated 16.7.2026 5. During the course of the hearing, learned counsel for the Applicant reiterated the submissions made in the Petition. Vide Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as “RoP”) dated 16.7.2026, the Applicant was directed to furnish, on an affidavit, the following information: Order in Petition No. 294/TD/2026 Page 2 of 8 a) The Auditor’s Report, in compliance with Regulations 3(3)(b), 6(1)(b), and 15(1)(d) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020; and b) The Audited Special Balance Sheet and Financial Statements, prepared in accordance with the financial reporting framework prescribed under the Companies Act, 2013, as on a date falling within 30 days immediately preceding the date of filing of the Petition. 6. In compliance with the RoP dated 16.7.2026, the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 22.10.2026, submitted the Audited Special Balance Sheet as on 30.4.2026 along with the Auditor’s Report. Hearing dated 23.10.2026 7. The matter was called out for the first hearing on 23.10.2026. The learned counsel for the Applicant submitted that the Applicant company has complied with the directions issued vide RoP dated 16.7.2026 and placed the affidavit on record. Considering the submissions, the matter was reserved for orders . Analysis and Decision 8. We have considered the submissions of the Applicant. Regulation 9(4) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading License and other Related Matters) Regulations, 2020 (the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020) provides as under: “(4) The Trading Licensee shall make an appropriate application accompanied by prescribed fees for up-gradation of its licence to a higher category or down- gradation of its licence to a lower category in order to fulfil the conditions of these regulations in accordance with the procedure specified in Regulation 15 of these regulations.” 9. Regulation 15(1) of the Trading Licence Regulations 2020 provides as under: Order in Petition No. 294/TD/2026 Page 3 of 8 trading licence and also the terms and conditions specified for Category ‘I’ trading licence. 15. Let an extract copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (Ministry of Power) and the Central Electricity Authority in terms of sub-section (7) of Section 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003, for their information and record. 16. We direct that the necessary endorsement be made on the licence issued to the applicant with regard to the change of Category of the licensee. 17. Petition No. 294/TD/2026 is allowed in terms of the above. Sd/- sd/- sd/- sd/- (Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V.)
